stories.headline: Trump says US will not attack Iran before midterm elections in November
stories.summary: The Trump administration has signaled it will not launch military action against Iran prior to November midterm elections, reducing near-term geopolitical escalation risk. This provides temporary clarity on Middle East tensions that have been driving oil and equity volatility.
stories.why_matters: De-escalation messaging reduces safe-haven flows and supports risk asset appetite in the near term.

stories.headline: Lufthansa, Indian airlines suspend flights to Riyadh after Houthi attacks
stories.summary: Major international carriers are suspending service to Saudi Arabia following escalating Houthi drone and missile strikes on Riyadh airport. The disruptions reflect ongoing regional instability and potential supply-chain risks in critical Middle East hubs.
stories.why_matters: Airlines and logistics are core to US supply chains and earnings; flight suspensions signal real operational friction from geopolitical risk.

stories.headline: German government raises growth forecasts for 2026 and 2027
stories.summary: Germany has upgraded its economic outlook for the next two years, signaling improved confidence in eurozone recovery and demand. The upgrade may support EUR strength and reduce deflationary pressure in the EU.
stories.why_matters: Stronger European growth supports global demand and reduces recession risk for US multinational earnings.

concept.title: The Risk-Off Equity Selloff vs. Safe-Haven Yield Decline
concept.one_liner: Stocks fall while bonds rally—a classic flight-to-quality pattern driven by geopolitical uncertainty and Fed hawkishness.
concept.explanation: Today's S&P 500 decline of -0.57% paired with a modest VIX uptick and simultaneous 4–5 bps drops in both 2Y and 10Y yields reveals a classic risk-off trade. Investors are rotating from equities into Treasuries despite Fed rate-hike signals, suggesting geopolitical concerns (Iran, Houthis, Middle East supply disruption) are overriding growth optimism. The slight USD strength (EUR/USD down 0.0063) reinforces the safety-trade narrative.

narrative: Equities retreated modestly on Middle East geopolitical tensions and Houthi escalation, prompting a flight to quality into Treasuries despite Fed rate-hike rhetoric; meanwhile, softer EUR/USD and yield curve flattening signal investor caution ahead of this week's inflation and labor data.
